Mark Cuban was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Pittsburgh is part of the U.S.
Cuban's father, Norton Cuban, was an automobile upholsterer.
Cuban's mother, Shirley (née Feldman), had a different job or career goal every other week.
Cuban is Jewish.
Cuban grew up in Mount Lebanon, a suburb of Pittsburgh.
Mount Lebanon is part of Pennsylvania.
Cuban came from a working-class family.
Cuban's paternal grandfather changed the surname from "Chabenisky" to "Cuban".
Cuban's maternal grandparents were Romanian Jewish immigrants according to his brother Brian.
Cuban's maternal grandmother was from Lithuania according to Mark Cuban himself.
Mark Cuban first ventured into business at age 12 by selling garbage bags.
A few years later, Cuban earned money by selling stamps and coins.
At age 16, Cuban took advantage of a Pittsburgh Post-Gazette strike by running newspapers from Cleveland to Pittsburgh.
Instead of attending high school for his senior year, Cuban enrolled as a full-time student at the University of Pittsburgh where he joined the Pi Lambda Phi fraternity.

After one year at the University of Pittsburgh, Cuban transferred to Indiana University in Bloomington and graduated from the Kelley School of Business with a Bachelor of Science degree in management in 1981.
Mark Cuban co-founded MicroSolutions with support from his previous customers at Your Business Software.
Initially, MicroSolutions operated as a systems integrator and software reseller.
The company was an early proponent of technologies such as Carbon Copy, Lotus Notes, and CompuServe.
One of the company's largest clients was Perot Systems.
MicroSolutions grew to more than $30 million in revenue.
In 1990, Cuban sold MicroSolutions to CompuServe—then a subsidiary of H&R Block—for $6 million (over $14.7 million today).
Cuban made approximately $2 million after taxes on the deal.
In 1995, Cuban and Todd Wagner joined Audionet.
Audionet became Broadcast.com in 1998.
By 1999, Broadcast.com had grown to 330 employees and $13.5 million in revenue for the second quarter.
Broadcast.com helped launch the first live-streamed Victoria's Secret Fashion Show that year.
In 1999, during the dot com boom, Broadcast.com was acquired by Yahoo! for $5.7 billion in Yahoo! stock.
Cuban hedged against the risk of a decline in the value of the Yahoo! shares he received from the sale.
Cuban financially supported Grokster in the Supreme Court case MGM v. Grokster.
Cuban is a partner in Synergy Sports Technology, a web-based basketball scouting and video delivery tool used by many NBA teams.
Mark Cuban invested $1.7 million in file-sharing company RedSwoosh in 2005.
Red Swoosh was acquired by Akamai for $19 million in 2007.
Cuban invested in IceRocket, a search engine that scours the blogosphere for content.
In 2003, Cuban started the Fallen Patriot Fund to help families of U.S. military personnel killed or injured during the Iraq War.
Cuban personally matched the first $1 million in contributions with funds from the Mark Cuban Foundation.
Cuban was featured on the cover of Best magazine's November 2003 premiere issue announcing the arrival of high-definition television.
Cuban co-founded AXS TV (formerly HDNet) with Philip Garvin, the first high-definition satellite television network.
In February 2004, Cuban announced that he would be working with ABC to produce a reality television series called The Benefactor.
The series premiered on September 13, 2004.
The series was canceled before the full season aired due to poor ratings.
Cuban is no. 190 on Forbes' list of "World's Richest People" with a net worth of $3.9 billion in 2018.
Cuban has been a "shark" investor on the ABC reality program Shark Tank since season two in 2011.
As of May 2015, he had invested in 85 deals across 111 Shark Tank episodes for a total of $19.9 million invested.
Cuban owns film distributor Magnolia Pictures.
Through Magnolia, Cuban financed Redacted, a fictional dramatization based on the 2006 Mahmudiyah killings, written and directed by Brian De Palma.
In April 2011, Cuban put Magnolia Pictures and Landmark Theatres up for sale but said he was happy to continue making money from the properties if they didn't get the price and premium they wanted.
Cuban has invested in cryptocurrency Dogecoin.
Cuban accepted Dogecoin as a method of payment for Dallas Mavericks merchandise and tickets since at least early 2021.
In January 2022, Mark Cuban launched the Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company with the aim of lowering generic drug prices for end consumers in the U.S.
On January 4, 2000, Cuban purchased a majority stake in the NBA's Dallas Mavericks for $285 million from H. Ross Perot Jr.
In the 20 years before Cuban bought the team, the Mavericks won only 40% of their games and had a playoff record of 21–32.
In the 10 years following, the team won 69% of their regular season games and reached the playoffs in each of those seasons except for one.
The Mavericks' playoff record with Cuban is 49–57, including their first trip to the NBA Finals in 2006 where they lost to the Miami Heat.
Cuban sits alongside fans while donning team jerseys when attending Dallas Mavericks games.
Cuban travels in his private Gulfstream V airplane to attend road games of the Dallas Mavericks.
In May 2010, H. Ross Perot Jr., who retained 5% ownership, filed a lawsuit against Cuban, alleging the franchise was insolvent or in imminent danger of insolvency.
In June 2010, Cuban responded in a court filing maintaining that Perot is wrongly seeking money to offset some $100 million in losses on the Victory Park real estate development.
The lawsuit was dismissed in 2011 due in part to Cuban asserting proper management of the team due to its recent victory in the 2011 NBA Finals.
In January 2018, Cuban announced that the Dallas Mavericks would accept Bitcoin as payment for tickets in the following season.
On March 4, 2021, Cuban announced that the Mavericks would begin accepting Dogecoin as payment for both merchandise and tickets to games.
Cuban decided to stop playing the National Anthem at Dallas Mavericks games in order to "respect those whose believed the anthem did not represent them."
He supported this movement as far back as late 2020.
The NBA responded by requiring every team to play it, citing it as their "long-standing policy."
On November 28, 2023, The Dallas Morning News reported that Cuban was in the process of selling his share in the Dallas Mavericks to Miriam Adelson.
On December 27, 2023, the NBA approved the sale of a controlling interest of 73% in the Dallas Mavericks to the Adelson and Dumont families.
Cuban has repeatedly expressed interest in owning a Major League Baseball franchise.
In 2008, he submitted an initial bid of $1.3 billion to buy the Chicago Cubs but was not selected for the final bidding process.
In August 2010, Cuban actively bid to buy the Texas Rangers with Jeffrey L. Beck but lost the deal before the Rangers played the San Francisco Giants in the 2010 World Series.
Cuban has expressed interest in becoming a minority owner of the New York Mets after owner Fred Wilpon announced he was planning to sell up to a 25% stake in the team.
Cuban wanted to purchase his hometown Pittsburgh Pirates but was rebuffed by then-owner Kevin McClatchy in 2005.
In 2005, Cuban expressed interest in buying the NHL's Pittsburgh Penguins.

In 2006, Cuban joined an investment group with Dan Marino, Kevin Millevoi, Andy Murstein, Gregg Perelman, and Todd Reidbord to attempt to acquire the Penguins but was ultimately rejected by team owners Mario Lemieux and Ronald Burkle.
Cuban has been a panelist at the annual MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference since 2009.
In April 2010, Cuban loaned the newly formed United Football League (UFL) $5 million.
He did not own a franchise and was not involved in day-to-day operations of the league or any of its teams.
Cuban is an admirer of author Ayn Rand. He found her novel The Fountainhead incredibly motivating.
His political views have leaned toward libertarianism.
Cuban held a position on the centrist Unity08 political organization's advisory council.
Despite leaning towards libertarianism, Cuban posted that paying more taxes to be the most patriotic thing someone can do.
In 2012, Cuban donated $7,000 to political campaigns with $6,000 going to Republican Senator Orrin Hatch of Utah and $1,000 to Democratic California Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren.
On February 8, 2008, Cuban voiced his support for the draft Bloomberg movement on his blog.

In November 2012, in response to Donald Trump offering President Obama $5 million to a charity of President Obama's choosing if he released passport applications and college transcripts to the public, Cuban offered Trump $1 million to a charity of Trump's choosing if Trump shaved his head.
On December 19, 2012, Cuban donated $250,000 to the Electronic Frontier Foundation to support its work on patent reform.
At the Code/Media conference in February 2015, Cuban said that having the FCC overseeing the Internet scares him.
Cuban formally endorsed Hillary Clinton for president at a July 30, 2016, rally in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
During that campaign stop, he criticized Republican nominee Donald Trump as "a jagoff."
On November 22, 2016, Cuban met with the then President-elect Trump's key advisor Steve Bannon.
In May 2020, Cuban voiced his support for former Vice President Joe Biden in the 2020 U.S. presidential election.
On February 2, 2021, Cuban joined Reddit's WallStreetBets "Ask Me Anything" forum and fielded user questions related to the GameStop short squeeze.
Prior to the 2024 Presidential election, Mark Cuban endorsed Kamala Harris for President, describing her as the only candidate in "founder mode."
Cuban started the Fallen Patriot Fund to help families of U.S. military personnel killed or injured during the Iraq War.
He personally matched the first $1 million in contributions with funds from the Mark Cuban Foundation.
In September 2015, Cuban stated that running for president was a fun idea to toss around and that he could beat both Trump and Clinton if he ran in the 2016 U.S. presidential election.
This was interpreted by many media outlets as an indication that he was considering running but he clarified soon afterward that he had no intention of doing so.
In October 2015, Cuban posted on Twitter that maybe he would run for Speaker of the House at the time there was no clear front-runner to replace the outgoing John Boehner.
Cuban told Meet the Press in May 2016 that he would be open to being Clinton's running mate but would seek to alter some of her positions if she were his running mate.
In July 2016, Cuban appeared on a live segment on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert entitled "Gloves Off: Mark Cuban Edition" in which he mocked Trump.
Cuban criticized Trump for not paying back into the system that allowed him to amass such wealth.

In September 2016, during a post-presidential debate interview, Cuban criticized Trump's characterization of paying the minimum required taxes as smart and criticized Trump for not paying back into the system that allowed him to amass such wealth.
In October 2017, Cuban said he would "definitely" run for president if he was single.
Later that month, Cuban claimed that if he ran for president in 2020, it would be as a Republican and described himself as "socially a centrist but very fiscally conservative."
In March 2019, Cuban stated that he was "strongly considering running" for president as an independent candidate.
In May 2019, Cuban said: "It would take the perfect storm for me to do it. There's some things that could open the door, but I'm not projecting or predicting it right now."
In June 2020, Cuban revealed that he had seriously considered running for president in 2020 as an independent candidate.
He commissioned a national poll which showed he would only receive 25 percent of the vote in a hypothetical matchup with President Donald Trump and former Vice President Joe Biden.
Cuban was fined by the NBA at least $1.665 million across 13 incidents, primarily for critical statements about the league and its referees.
In June 30, 2006, interview, Mavericks player Dirk Nowitzki said that Cuban needs to learn how to control himself as well as the players do.
Cuban matches NBA fines with charitable donations of equal amounts.
In a nationally publicized incident in 2002, he criticized the league's manager of officials, Ed T. Rush, saying that he "wouldn't be able to manage a Dairy Queen."
Dairy Queen management invited him to manage a Dairy Queen restaurant for a day.
During the 2005–06 NBA season, Cuban started a booing campaign when former Mavericks player Michael Finley returned to play against the Mavericks as a member of the San Antonio Spurs.
In a playoff series between the Mavericks and Spurs, Cuban cursed Spurs forward Bruce Bowen and was fined $25,000 by the NBA for rushing onto the court and criticizing NBA officials.
After the 2006 NBA Finals, Cuban was fined $250,000 by the NBA for repeated misconduct following the Mavericks' loss to the Miami Heat in Game Five of the 2006 NBA Finals.
In February 2007, Cuban publicly criticized NBA Finals MVP Dwyane Wade and declared that he would get fined if he made any comments about what he thought really happened in the 2006 NBA Finals.
On January 16, 2009, the league fined Cuban $25,000 for yelling at Denver Nuggets player J. R. Smith at the end of the first half on a Mavericks-at-Nuggets game played on January 13.
Cuban offered to match the fine with a donation to a charity of Smith's choosing.

In May 2009, Cuban made a reference to the Denver Nuggets being "thugs" after a loss to the Nuggets in game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals. The statement was geared towards the Nuggets and their fans.
On January 18, 2014, Cuban was fined $100,000 for confronting referees and using inappropriate language toward them.
In February 2018, Cuban was fined $600,000 by the NBA for stating that the Dallas Mavericks should "tank for the rest of the season."
Commissioner Adam Silver stated that the fine was "for public statements detrimental to the NBA."
On March 6, 2020, Cuban was fined $500,000 by the NBA for "public criticism and detrimental conduct regarding NBA officiating," according to the league.
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed a civil suit against Cuban relating to alleged insider trading in the shares of Mamma.com.
A stock dilution occurred shortly after a trade in June 2004, giving hints of inside knowledge at the time of the trade, and Cuban allegedly was saved from a loss of $750,000.
In July 2009, the U.S. District Court dismissed the charges against Cuban.
The SEC appealed the decision.
In September 2010, an appeals court said that the district court had erred and that further proceedings would be necessary to address the merits of the suit.
A federal jury in Texas found in favor of Cuban on October 16, 2013. The nine-member jury issued the verdict after deliberating for 3 hours and 35 minutes.
In March 2014, Cuban was on air at CNBC criticizing high-frequency trading (HFT).
In a March 6, 2018, article, Willamette Week reported an alleged April 2011 incident between Cuban and a female patron of a Portland, Oregon bar called the Barrel Room.
The woman told Portland police that Cuban sexually groped her while she posed for pictures with him.

Cuban denied the allegations, and his attorney provided the results of a polygraph test taken by Cuban and written statements from two medical doctors stating that the actions described were anatomically improbable.
The Portland District Attorney's office declined to prosecute, citing a lack of concrete evidence to support the claim and the woman's preference not to proceed with charges.
